The designated extraction point at the edge of the zone - a marked gate or pad the player has to reach before time runs out
Interconnected industrial yards and urban districts on one map, streets and alleys running between them

layout_placement.text: Valuable loot crates and hidden stashes spread through the zone, some obvious and some concealed
Where AI enemy combatants enter and the ground they patrol, concentrated on the loot-heavy zones
The extraction trigger, ending the run and banking whatever the player is carrying
Deploy points at the zone edges, screened so a player is not in a firing line on arrival
A contracting play boundary over the match

mechanics: Fast fluid movement
High quality gunplay with realistic recoil, aim down sights, reloading and weapon customization
Loadout system choosing primary, secondary, tactical gear and armour before deploying
Match flow: spawn in, complete objectives, gather resources, fight off threats, extract within a time limit
Risk versus reward - lose all items if you die before extracting
Team support options
Kill feed and match HUD
Mobile friendly touch controls
First person camera
Smooth performance on gritty modern visuals
notes: No extraction preset exists. Took Battle Royale for its open map, world loot and interiors, and swapped in the extraction point from Survival gate-escape, which is the only row that expresses a boundary exit that ends the run.
boundary-shrinking came with the preset and the prompt never mentions a closing ring - it has a time limit instead. Kept per instruction and labelled, but it is the pick most likely to be wrong.
P3 because the industrial and urban buildings are entered rather than fought around.
Extent and detail pull apart here: large open zones plus concealed loot inside rooms cannot both be framed in one render. Band set to district and the split offered as a question.

open_questions.ask: What is the smallest thing you want to be able to pick out - loot crates inside rooms, whole warehouses and streets, or districts and main roads across the zone?
What is the extraction point - a helicopter pad, a vehicle, or a gate at the edge of the map?
Are the industrial area and the urban district one continuous map, or separate maps you deploy into?
Do the objectives sit in fixed places I can build around, or move from match to match?

notes_for_us: Extraction shooters are a large current category and there is no preset for one. The parts exist - open battlefield, world loot, an exit that ends the run - but the exit is filed in Survival, so a Shooter that only loads its own file cannot find the single most important place in the mode.

The prompt says objectives without saying what or where. Objectives are the spatial half of a match flow and neither an option nor a question form covers them, so they went to mechanics and the map has nothing standing for them.
Mobile touch controls and a kill feed are clearly not ours and step 0 handles that cleanly. Worth recording that this prompt was well served by the triage rule rather than hurt by it.

skill_gap.name: no extraction mode
skill_gap.why: the mode has no preset and its defining feature, an exit that banks your loot, exists only as a Survival row, so a Shooter build reaches it only by going to the shared catalogue

image_prompt.text: Caves, hollows and burrows across the map that an animal claims and returns to
Distinctive natural landmarks - a lone rock, a dead tree, a waterfall - so an animal can navigate a huge map by sight
An open clearing where animals congregate
Rivers and lakes across the map to drink from, deep enough for fish to live in

layout_placement.text: Food sources scattered across the map - plants, carcasses and prey - placed so an animal has to keep moving to eat
Where the hostile AI animals enter and the ground they roam - fish in the water, birds above, dinosaurs and predators on land

mechanics: You play as one animal and stay as it until death
Death comes from other animals or from failing to eat or drink
Hunger and thirst as survival pressure
AI animals, fish, dinosaurs and birds hunt the player
Other players can kill you too
notes: Two genres because the space is an animal sim and the loop is survival. Roleplay leads on the shape - an animal sim has no settlement - and Survival contributes the food, water and predator rows.
Rejected Survival world-biomes even though threat across a huge map is what it describes, because the prompt calls it one huge map and that shape routes P4. Kept as one continuous surface.
CHECK on the water because fish swimming and birds flying are volumetric; fine as a play-height envelope unless the user wants real underwater or aerial play, which is asked.
Huge map plus food items on the ground is the extent-versus-detail conflict; band set to region and the question asked rather than assumed.

open_questions.ask: What is the smallest thing you want to be able to pick out - individual food items and dens, single trees and rocks, whole clearings and rivers, or coastlines and forests?
Which environments should the map hold - forest, plains, rivers and lakes, mountains, or a mix of all of them?
Do you actually swim underwater as a fish and fly as a bird, or are those only AI animals you see?
Should dinosaurs share the map with modern animals, or is it one or the other?

captured: one huge map
food and water sources spread across it
AI fish, birds, dinosaurs and land animals that hunt the player
other players as a threat
you stay as one animal until death

preset_rejected.why: the prompt is a world where every other animal and player is trying to kill you, so a gathering area for animals to congregate in works against what it describes - kept as a clearing rather than a safe hub

notes_for_us: The prompt says huge map and nothing about what is in it, which is exactly the case where the scale question is worth spending. It also means biome composition - the biggest visual decision in the build - is unanswerable, and no option can hold a list of biomes on one continuous map. world-biomes would, and it costs the P4 the prompt rules out.

Hostile animals and ambient animals are the same creatures here. spawner-npc is written for combat emitters and npc-population is explicitly non-hostile, so a world whose wildlife is both had to pick one.

den-shelter and social-hub both arrived with the preset and only one survives contact with the prompt. The instruction to keep both and label them is followed, but on a survival prompt a congregating hub is a real risk to the build.

unmatched_options.text: a huge map with varied environments implied but never named
you are an animal and stay as that animal until death
you die from not drinking or eating
AI fish, dinosaurs and birds that try to kill you, alongside other players

skill_gap.name: no hostile ambient wildlife
skill_gap.why: the animals are scenery, threat and prey at once, and the network splits those across spawner-npc for emitters and npc-population for life explicitly limited to non-hostile, with nothing covering both

image_prompt.text: Recesses and doorways cut into the hallway walls, the only places to break a monster line of sight in a corridor this narrow
Monstrous figures packed densely along both sides of the hallway, some partly blocking the way through
A single cramped hallway repeating forward without end - the same walls, ceiling and lights recurring

layout_placement.text: Where the monsters come from along the hallway and the stretch of corridor each one holds
Small pickups found along the corridor

notes: interior-endless carries P6 because the corridor continues without a boundary and the structure has to be valid by construction; not overridable.
The prompt answers the endless-or-bounded question outright, so that one was not asked.
collectible-nodes came with the preset and the prompt says nothing about anything to pick up.
The monsters are described as filling the space rather than entering it. spawner-npc holds where they come from; their density as geometry had to ship as free text.

notes_for_us: Cramped with monsters means the monsters are the density of the space, not an emitter feeding it. spawner-npc is the only hostile row and it answers a different question, so the central image of a nine-word prompt ships as free text with no route.

A corridor this narrow makes cover-los almost self-contradictory: the row wants cutouts at least four studs deep on the entry axis and the prompt wants the hallway cramped. Kept it and said so, but the two constraints pull apart.
Room is the honest band for a corridor and endless is the honest extent, and the four bands cannot describe a space that is small in two dimensions and unbounded in the third.
